title: Global Employment Research — Quantitative Visualisations
scope: Curated numeric evidence extracted from the complete Notion research export. Every chart includes its source, period, unit and limitation.

charts.title: India: sector share of GVA
charts.subtitle: 2024–25 · share of gross value added
charts.source: NITI Aayog, India’s Services Sector: Insights from GVA Trends and State-Level Dynamics
charts.note: These are output/GVA shares, not employment shares. Rounded figures; do not use them as a jobs distribution.

charts.title: Services share of employment rose
charts.subtitle: India · 1992 to 2022
charts.note: An 7.9 percentage-point increase between the two reported years. This is not a year-by-year time series.

charts.title: Entry-level share in one job-listing sample
charts.subtitle: PrepNPlaced indexed Indian tech listings · May–July vs October 2026
charts.note: The sample reported 908/15,429 entry/junior listings earlier and 799/18,752 in October. This is one publisher’s indexed sample, not a census of Indian vacancies; source coverage/classification may change.

charts.title: IT-BPM fresher hiring outlook
charts.subtitle: India · FY2026 estimate vs FY2027 forecast
charts.source: Economic Times, 14 October 2026, citing HAN Digital outlook
charts.note: FY2027 is a forecast, not realised hiring. This covers IT-BPM fresher hiring broadly, not AI-only jobs.

charts.title: India’s share of global exports increased
charts.subtitle: 2005 vs 2024 · merchandise and commercial services
charts.source: Government of India, Economic Survey 2025–26, Chapter 4 and Chapter 8
charts.note: The two categories are distinct. Values represent India’s share of world exports, not growth rates.

charts.title: Backward global value-chain participation
charts.subtitle: Foreign value added as a share of gross exports
charts.note: India’s ratio rose then moderated. Vietnam is shown only for 2020; missing years are intentionally not interpolated. This is one measure of GVC integration, not a complete competitiveness score.

charts.title: Reported association: exports and outcomes
charts.subtitle: World Bank cross-country sample, 1995–2019 · associated change for a 10% export increase
charts.source: World Bank, Leveraging Trade for More and Better Jobs
charts.note: These are reported cross-country associations, not guaranteed causal effects and not an India-specific forecast. Do not interpret as a causal elasticity.

charts.title: Global trade in goods and services
charts.subtitle: 2025 · WTO World Trade Statistics
charts.note: The research also reports total world goods and commercial services trade of US$34.65 trillion, with services representing 27.6%. Growth rates are not absolute trade values.

special.title: India IT & BPM exports
special.note: Industry estimate; definitions and reporting dates may differ from other industry totals.

special.title: GCC revenue in India
special.note: Ecosystem revenue, not current job openings.

special.title: GCC count in India
special.note: Centre count, not a count of distinct employers hiring today.

special.title: India tech startup funding
special.note: Funding is not revenue, profit, or a guarantee of hiring.

special.title: Management experiment in India
special.period: Average productivity increase in treatment plants
special.source: Bloom et al., Does Management Matter? Evidence from India, World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 5573
special.note: Experiment covered 28 plants across 17 firms. This should not be generalised as an 11% gain for every Indian business.

special.title: IT-BPM industry revenue
special.source: IBEF, IT & BPM Industry in India
special.note: Industry estimate; do not add overlapping industry categories.

special.title: World goods + services trade
special.note: Global aggregate, not India's trade value.

integrity: No synthetic salary distributions or invented employer pay comparisons are plotted.
GVA share is not employment share.
Forecasts are labelled as forecasts; they are not actual outcomes.
Cross-country associations are not described as causal effects.
The 99-row personal job-tracker snapshot is separate from national labour-market evidence and is not used as a representative India-wide dataset.
All charts are drawn from numeric claims already recorded in the Notion research export; see the source links and caveats beneath each chart.
